skills.name: ask-matt
skills.short: Routes you to the right user-invoked skill.
skills.summary: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the user-invoked skills in this repo.
skills.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.short: Reproduce, minimise, hypothesise, instrument, fix, regression-test.
skills.summary: Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions: build a feedback loop that goes red on this bug → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test.
skills.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.

skills.name: grill-with-docs
skills.short: Grilling that also builds the domain model: GLOSSARY.md and ADRs.
skills.summary: Grilling session that also builds your project's domain model, sharpening terminology and updating `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs inline.
skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

skills.name: triage
skills.short: Moves issues through a state machine of triage roles.
skills.summary: Move issues through a state machine of triage roles.
skills.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.short: Finds deepening opportunities, shows an HTML report, then grills you on one.
skills.summary: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.
skills.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

skills.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
skills.short: Issue tracker, labels, doc layout. Once per repo.
skills.summary: Configure this repo for the engineering skills (issue tracker, triage labels, domain doc layout). Run once per repo.
skills.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

skills.name: tdd
skills.short: Red-green-refactor, one vertical slice at a time.
skills.summary: Test-driven development with a red-green-refactor loop. Builds features or fixes bugs one vertical slice at a time.
skills.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

skills.name: to-spec
skills.short: Turns the conversation into a spec in your issue tracker.
skills.summary: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker.
skills.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

skills.name: to-tickets
skills.short: Breaks a plan into tracer-bullet tickets with blocking edges.
skills.summary: Break any plan, spec, or conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, whether as text in a local file or as native blocking links on a real tracker.
skills.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

skills.name: wayfinder
skills.short: Work too big for one session, as a map of decision tickets.
skills.summary: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on the issue tracker, resolved one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.
skills.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

skills.name: implement
skills.short: Builds a spec or tickets with /tdd at seams, closes with /code-review.
skills.summary: Build the work described by a spec or set of tickets, driving `/tdd` at pre-agreed seams and closing out with `/code-review` before committing.
skills.description: Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.

skills.name: implement-spec
skills.short: A whole spec on one integration branch, with parallel subagents.
skills.summary: Implement a whole spec on one integration branch. Works the tickets as a task graph, running implementer subagents across the ready frontier for maximum concurrency, then closes out with `/code-review`.
skills.description: Implement the result of /to-spec and /to-tickets in code.

skills.name: prototype
skills.short: A throwaway prototype to answer a design question.
skills.summary: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question: a single shareable HTML file for state/logic, or several toggleable UI variations.
skills.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

skills.name: research
skills.short: Primary-source research saved as a cited Markdown file.
skills.summary: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a cited Markdown file in the repo, run as a background agent.
skills.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.short: Sharpens terminology and keeps GLOSSARY.md and ADRs current.
skills.summary: Actively build and sharpen a project's domain model by challenging terms, stress-testing with scenarios, and updating `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs inline.
skills.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.short: Shared vocabulary for deep modules with small interfaces.
skills.summary: Shared discipline and vocabulary for designing deep modules: small interfaces, clean seams, testable through the interface.
skills.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

skills.name: code-review
skills.short: Standards and Spec reviews of the diff, in parallel.
skills.summary: Two-axis review of the diff since a fixed point: **Standards** (does it follow the repo's coding standards, plus a Fowler smell baseline?) and **Spec** (does it faithfully implement the originating issue/spec?), run as parallel sub-agents.
skills.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

skills.name: pr
skills.short: PR body: summary, before/after evidence, merge-danger call.
skills.summary: The shape a pull request body should take: a summary as the smallest visual that makes the change clear, before/after evidence that it works, and a merge-danger call (one-way or two-way door, plus blast radius).
skills.description: Use when writing a PR body.

skills.name: retro
skills.short: After a session, suggests environment fixes, worst first.
skills.summary: Suggest improvements to the coding agent's environment (navigation, automated checks, coding standards, steering files, tooling) after a session, most severe first.
skills.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

skills.name: wizard
skills.short: An interactive bash wizard for steps only a human can do.
skills.summary: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform: provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover.
skills.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.short: Interviews you about any plan until every branch is resolved.
skills.summary: Get relentlessly interviewed about a plan or design until every branch of the design tree is resolved.
skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

skills.name: grilling
skills.short: The reusable interview primitive behind the grill skills.
skills.summary: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea until every branch of the design tree is resolved.
skills.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

skills.name: handoff
skills.short: Compacts the conversation into a doc for another agent.
skills.summary: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document so another agent can continue the work.
skills.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

skills.name: teach
skills.short: Teaches a concept over several sessions in this directory.
skills.summary: Teach the user a new skill or concept over multiple sessions, using the current directory as a stateful teaching workspace.
skills.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

skills.name: to-questionnaire
skills.short: Turns a decision you can't make alone into a questionnaire.
skills.summary: Turn a decision you can't answer alone into a Markdown questionnaire for the one person who can (filled in async, or together over a meeting).
skills.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

skills.name: wait-what
skills.short: Re-explains a message that didn't land, in glossary terms.
skills.summary: Fire this the moment a message doesn't land. The agent re-pitches it with the context you're missing, in plain English, using your `GLOSSARY.md` vocabulary.
skills.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

skills.name: writing-for-agents
skills.short: How to write skills, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md.
skills.summary: Writing documents for agents: skills, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, and any doc an agent reaches by a pointer.
skills.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
